runs.t: All 18 original inspector reports for the initial licences assessed an environmental liabilities risk assessment, a closure, restoration and aftercare management plan, and financial provision as unnecessary at the application stage (Supplementary Table 3). For P1191-01 this assessment appears on page 20. P1191 subsequently appeared on the requirements list for December 2025. The operator’s letter of 22 September 2026 states that the Agency had asked on 24 August 2026 for a plan to complete the closure plan, the liabilities risk assessment and financial provision, and it asks the Agency to reconsider that request. The Agency’s own letter and any subsequent final determination were not obtained.

Records of the operating stage exist for these licences. The annual environmental reports for 2025, available for 16 of the 18, record 56 incident notifications across 12 licences. The reports class them in different ways, among them releases of refrigerant gas, trigger levels reached in storm water and exceedances of discharge limits, and a trigger level reached is not an exceedance of a limit. The count takes the figure in the incident table of each report (Supplementary Table 7). Two reports are internally inconsistent: for P1184 the table gives five and the narrative four, and for P1187 the table gives two and another section states none. Using the narrative figures for those two reports gives 53 notifications across 11 licences. Soil and groundwater were sampled at three licensed sites of one operator in 2025 and 2026. The baseline reports for those sites, as read in text, give no values by sampling point, so no measurement could be paired with a baseline, and no change in site condition can be inferred in either direction. These are observations of the operating stage. They are not measurements of the condition of a site after closure, and the tracked closure cases provide none. Separately, the emissions-trading reports for the Equinix DB5 permit give reported emissions from fossil-fuel combustion of 785.62, 29,231.72 and 363.76 tonnes CO₂e in 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. EdgeConneX permit IE-GHG186-04 records retirement of twelve gas generators in November 2022. These operational records do not measure post-closure site condition.

Table 3 | Stages documented in 27 tracking records. The 27 rows include a permit surrender (C02), a rebuild (C05), a planned closure (C12) and a partial exit (C26), which are tracked records and not completed closures. Demolition is counted as stated complete where a source says so (C04, C06, C07, C24) and as qualified where the source is internally inconsistent (C08) or completion is inferred from later construction (C09). Amount recorded counts the records in which a source gives an amount in connection with exit, relocation or closure. The five amounts are of different kinds, are not all restoration costs and are listed with their nature in Supplementary Table 5. The last column counts records that identify the party that bore the final net cost of environmental restoration. No record does so, and no final account of the works was identified. For seven records with project-level documents, the documents reviewed do not identify it; for the other 20 the available sources describe the event and do not support an assessment. Both verdicts and their basis are given for each record in Supplementary Table 1. The denominator includes tracking records for events other than completed closures.
